comments.author: theFEARhunterZ
comments.body_html: The biggest factor that affects how quick a bot can track you is hearing distance. I’m no expert but the AI here seem to track based on a last known. Once a bot becomes aware of your position, it instantly locks onto you (regardless of obstacles). The vision speed values just determine how quick the bot goes from “seeing” you to shooting you. Best way to slow their detection speed down is to reduce how far out they can hear you.

comments.author: suff
comments.body_html:
I’m still learning and need more trying before I can give solid feedback, but main points of feedbacks so far (and I’m not sure profile is fully responsible for it):
1. After you’ve been visually spotted (or group spotted), even if you repositioned 20+ meters from initial position, low level gear scavs quite often get an immidiate successful shot with inhumane reaction characteristics as soon as you get in their view on ranges about 30 meters. For low level players of Realism Mod it’s often fatal.
2. Group spotting seems to share information about you to far away members (50-70m), and then they start suppressing you without being able to see. Experience it in heavy rain from a group of scavs where one is close and one in the end of the central woods sawmill
3. Investigating close gunfire scavs are quite reckless and inattentive to the possible threat

4. Goon squad on woods has very high spotting ability
5. Looting seems quite loud, I experienced many times that as soon as I open a container, the bot sprints to my position

I have some recordings done with Raid Review if you interested in any of the points

comments.author: adishee
comments.body_html:
Thank you for elaborating a bit on that.

I’ve noticed that bots sometimes are a little too oblivious for hearing – and with my new visual nerf mod, I guess hearing could be buffed.

I will work on the 360 no-scoping. Perhaps it’s a little overtuned. (Although I might add something to the aforementioned visual mod that decreases accuracy as a function of viability, so I would have to balance Adibots to that as well).

comments.author: adishee
comments.body_html:
Thanks for the solid feedback. Keep in mind that I have almost no time to playtest these things usually so you all are playtesting for me, essentially.

1) I intended for the Scavs to fire very quickly after seeing you, and very inaccurately, so I’ll work on that. I think I’ve seen a variable for reacquire after reposition.

2) I will explore the SAIN options to see if there is some kind of communication variable, as I’ve also noticed that Scav swarming can get a little too much. But if there is a gunfight and nearby Scavs hear it, won’t it be obvious? Here is the importance of suppressed and subsonic. I will keep an eye out for these behaviors.

3) They’re cracked out crazies, that makes sense. HOWEVER, I do want to do a repass on Scav personalities (perhaps Scav-only personalities) to make give them a great diversity in personality.
